source.section: TC-40 lines 4 to 22 (Instructions PDF p.9 Line 4; PDF p.10 Lines 5 to 20 and the Line 17 table; PDF p.11 Line 22); (AJ) Military Retirement Credit (PDF p.23) and worksheet lines 1 and 2 (PDF p.24)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = military retirement pay (person 0) 20,000.00 = 20,000.00. Federal taxable income = 20,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 4,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Utah starts from federal AGI). TC-40 (single): line 4 federal AGI 20,000.00. Line 5 additions: none, 0.00. Line 6 = 20,000.00 + 0.00 = 20,000.00. Line 7 state tax refund 0.00. Line 8 subtractions 0.00. Line 9 Utah taxable income = 20,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 20,000.00. Line 10 = 20,000.00 x 0.045 = 900.00. Lines 11 to 16, by the projection: no dependents; the deduction on line 12 is held as the cap 15,750.00; initial credit = 0.06 x min(line 9 20,000.00, cap 15,750.00) = 0.06 x 15,750.00 = 945.00. Line 17 base phase-out amount 18,213.00. Line 18 = max(0, 20,000.00 - 18,213.00) = 1,787.00. Line 19 = 1,787.00 x 0.013 = 23.231. Line 20 = max(0, 945.00 - 23.231) = 921.769. Line 21 worksheet: line 1 federal AGI 20,000.00; line 2 standard deduction 15,750.00; line 3 senior deduction 0.00 (no amount in Utah's sources); line 4 15,750.00; line 5 = max(0, 20,000.00 - 15,750.00) = 4,250.00. Line 5 is above zero, so not exempt; line 21 blank. TC-40A Part 3: Military Retirement Credit Worksheet: line 1 20,000.00; line 2 = 20,000.00 x 0.045 = 900.00. Line 22 and TC-40A Part 3: line 20 921.769 + AJ 900.000 = 1,821.769, limited to the tax 900.00 (nonrefundable, PDF p.11 Line 24), so credits are 900.00. relief_amounts gives each credit's worksheet figure before that limit. Tax = 900.00 - 900.00 = 0.00. Line 20 already cancels the tax; AJ is nonrefundable and 'You may not carry forward or back any credit that is more than your tax liability' (PDF p.24). Expected lines are the formula results rounded to the cent at the end (half up); the three-decimal figures above are unrounded.
